copy.body:
In June, Roblox appointed SuperAwesome as its sole global vendor for advertising to under-13 users. The mandate: contextual-only targeting, zero persistent identifiers, no behavioral tracking. SuperAwesome's CEO Kate O'Loughlin put it simply: "We believe in powering a better internet for the next generation wherever they are."

Most of the industry will read that as a constraint to route around. I read it as validation.

We never tracked anyone to get our numbers.

In one 5-day activation, 40,000 players sent us 600,000+ messages across 160+ countries — unprompted. No survey, no incentive, no tracking pixel. They told us which competitor brands they already loved, what they thought of a product in real time, and when they were ready to buy — all volunteered in conversation.

That's not a workaround for COPPA. That's the actual product. The data layer inside every Roblox experience is extraordinary — the problem is nobody's built the infrastructure to capture it. Studios report on awareness. We extract intent.

It holds up under pressure too, not just in the ideal case. In one campaign, DAU had dropped 8% and was flattening. We deployed our Player Intelligence agents mid-campaign, on day 13 — and DAU rose +55%, daily visits rose +67%, daily impressions rose +157%, with the campaign's highest single-day user count landing on its final day.

Roblox just made the compliant path the only path for under-13 advertising. Turns out it was already the effective one. If your Gen Alpha strategy depends on tracking a nine-year-old, June was your warning shot.

Let's talk.
